## Interpretation (calibrated)

1. **One object? No — a hierarchy of estimands, with a confound now measured.** The joint and marginal prefix operators agree far above chance but disagree beyond fold noise (raw cos 0.474 vs self 0.84+). The registered consequence applies: cross-arm geometry claims here are descriptive. The right mental model from the four arms is not "one shared write-side operator at different grains" (H1's hope) but "per-conditioning conditional-expectation operators that share output structure (37° output angles vs 84–87° null) while their input geometries differ" — with part of that difference possibly attributable to the sparse-crossing identification gap itself. 2. **What the query unlocks is almost everything, per-answer.** Bare query R² 0.717 of 0.812 (context); per-trait 0.74–0.83 of 0.87–0.92. 3. **The context map is high-rank.** Hundreds of held-out-validated channels (≥700 even under the conservative positive-R² convention) refute the O(tens) picture the channel-count hypothesis carried; "a small number of channels carry almost all predictable variance" is false at per-answer grain.
